features.name: amp
features.description: PyTorch Automatic Mixed Precision (torch.amp) for training. Use autocast for Tensor Core-friendly forward and loss computation with FP16 or BF16, keep numerically sensitive reductions/metrics/export in FP32, and use GradScaler for FP16 so small gradients remain representable.
features.design_summary: Use supported FP16/BF16 autocast for training, GradScaler for FP16, and FP32 for sensitive reductions, metrics and exports.
features.how_to_use: PyTorch Automatic Mixed Precision (torch.amp) for training. Use autocast for Tensor Core-friendly forward and loss computation with FP16 or BF16, keep numerically sensitive reductions/metrics/export in FP32, and use GradScaler for FP16 so small gradients remain representable.
recommended_patterns: Wrap forward and loss computation in torch.amp.autocast for FP16 or BF16 mixed precision.
Use GradScaler for FP16 training; keep it optional or disabled for BF16.
Keep validation metrics, sklearn/NumPy/pandas work, and submission exports in FP32.
avoid_patterns: Do not treat FP8, FP4, INT8, or FP64 as the default AMP training-speed path.
Do not call .cpu().numpy() directly on low-precision prediction tensors; cast prediction/logit/probability tensors to float32 first.
features.model_shape_limitations: The autocast dtype must itself be allowed for the target architecture.
features.sample_code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
model = nn.Linear(64, 32).to(device)
opt = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
x = torch.randn(8, 64, device=device)
y = torch.randn(8, 32, device=device)
opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
with torch.autocast(device_type='cuda' if device == 'cuda' else 'cpu', dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    out = model(x)
    loss = (out - y).pow(2).mean()
loss.backward()
opt.step()

features.name: fp16
features.description: Hardware-native FP16 Tensor Core mixed-precision training. Use AMP/autocast for forward and backward computation, framework-managed FP32 optimizer state, and loss scaling when gradients would otherwise underflow.
features.design_summary: Use FP16 autocast for eligible operations with GradScaler, FP32 model parameters and optimizer state, and FP32 sensitive reductions and metrics. Preserve the model design and retain an FP32 fallback; accept a speed optimization only after a matching task-quality comparison.
features.how_to_use: Hardware-native FP16 Tensor Core mixed-precision training. Use AMP/autocast for forward and backward computation, framework-managed FP32 optimizer state, and loss scaling when gradients would otherwise underflow.
recommended_patterns: Use FP16 through AMP/autocast rather than manually converting the whole training loop to half precision.
Use GradScaler or framework automatic loss scaling for FP16 training.
Keep reductions, fragile losses, validation metrics, and export paths in FP32 when needed for accuracy.
avoid_patterns: Do not run optimizer updates only on FP16 weights when FP32 master weights or optimizer state are needed for accuracy.
Do not skip loss scaling for FP16 networks that show underflow, NaNs, divergence, or accuracy loss.
features.model_shape_limitations: Tensor Core-friendly matrix dimensions are required for best speed; retain FP32 islands for fragile operations.
features.sample_code:
import torch
cc = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
generation = {
    (7, 0): '1gen (Volta)',     (7, 5): '2gen (Turing)',
    (8, 0): '3gen (Ampere DC)', (8, 6): '3gen (Ampere)',
    (8, 9): '4gen (Ada)',       (9, 0): '4gen (Hopper)',
    (10, 0): '5gen (Blackwell DC)', (12, 0): '5gen (Blackwell GeForce)',
}.get(cc, f'unknown (CC {cc[0]}.{cc[1]})')
print(f'GPU CC={cc[0]}.{cc[1]}, tensor core {generation}')
print(f'compiled archs: {torch.cuda.get_arch_list()}')

features.name: tensor_cores
features.description:
Set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True so that when a cuDNN
convolution is called with a new set of size parameters, cuDNN runs
multiple algorithms, benchmarks them to find the fastest one, and
reuses it for the rest of the process for the same size parameters.
Disabling it (benchmark=False) makes cuDNN deterministically select
an algorithm, possibly at the cost of reduced performance. The
separate torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic flag controls
reproducibility and is distinct from the benchmark setting; combine
it with seeded RNGs (Python, NumPy, PyTorch) when you need
reproducible runs.
features.design_summary: For repeated convolution shapes, cuDNN benchmark mode can reuse a selected algorithm; deterministic execution is a separate setting and must follow the task reproducibility requirements.
features.how_to_use:
